title: The Room Between Two People

voiceProfile.pov: Close third-person alternating between Nandini and Siddharth, moving fluidly with chapter transitions
voiceProfile.tense: Past tense with close present-sensory domestic textures
voiceProfile.register: Restrained, architecturally observant, psychologically forensic, quiet and domestic
voiceProfile.narratorDistance: Intimate third-person, never judging, charting spatial distance as emotional distance
distinctiveDevices: Rooms, doorways, hallways, and domestic objects as instruments of measurement
Exact domestic expenses, lease amounts, and square footage details
Subtle shifts in morning routines indicating seasonal emotional weather

protagonist1.name: Nandini Rao
protagonist1.family: Daughter of a retired CPWD engineer in Mysore and a Carnatic music teacher; elder sister to Ananya (married, living in Chicago)
protagonist1.education: Masters in Art History & Textile Conservation from MS University, Baroda
protagonist1.career: Senior Conservator at the Heritage Textile Trust, Bangalore; restores heirloom Mysore silk, kalamkari temple hangings, and pre-independence khadi
habits: Checks room humidity with a small brass hygrometer kept on her vanity table
Washes her hands twice with unscented soap before touching any book or archival fabric
Drinks boiled water with two bruised cardamoms at 10 PM each evening
protagonist1.beliefs: Believes that damage rarely happens in explosions; it happens through chronic ambient light, slight chemical changes, and slow neglect
protagonist1.fears: That she has organized her life so carefully against sudden grief that she has eliminated joy
protagonist1.flaws: Uses professional composure and meticulous cataloging as armor to avoid confrontation; withdraws into silence rather than naming what hurts
protagonist1.speechStyle: Low-toned, measured, precise with adjectives, avoids superlatives, speaks slightly slower when angry
protagonist1.secrets: Kept a draft of a single-occupancy rental agreement for a 1BHK apartment in Cooke Town on her work laptop for five months
protagonist1.memories: The rain in Baroda in 2013 when Siddharth brought her four dry envelopes of Japanese mulberry paper wrapped inside his raincoat

protagonist2.name: Siddharth Mehta
protagonist2.family: Son of a cloth merchant in Ahmedabad who went bankrupt in 2001; mother lives with his elder brother in Gandhinagar
protagonist2.education: B.Arch from CEPT, Ahmedabad; M.Arch in Urban Heritage Conservation
protagonist2.career: Independent conservation architect; consults on colonial bungalow restorations, heritage precinct mappings in South India
protagonist2.income: Fluctuates between ₹90,000 and ₹2,40,000/month depending on consultancy disbursements
habits: Measures room dimensions by pacing with standard 30-inch strides when nervous
Sharpens 2B pencils with a surgical scalpel rather than a plastic sharpener
Leaves half-drunk cups of black tea on window ledges and bookshelves
protagonist2.beliefs: Believes buildings remember their inhabitants longer than inhabitants remember each other; believes repair is always nobler than demolition
protagonist2.fears: Fears becoming his father: financially unpredictable, carrying quiet shame into old age
protagonist2.flaws: Treats emotional tension like a structural settlement issue that will stabilise if left unprovoked; postpones hard conversations
protagonist2.speechStyle: Warm, analytical, prone to drawing diagrams on paper napkins when explaining feelings, self-effacing humor under stress
protagonist2.secrets: Lost ₹4,80,000 on a client default in late 2024 and took an emergency overdraft rather than tell Nandini during her mother's illness
protagonist2.memories: Watching Nandini stretch a fragile 18th-century woven border on a mounting board with acupuncture pins in 2017 without her hands shaking once

timeline.2011: Meet at an archaeological survey camp in Champaner; both in their mid-twenties
timeline.2015: Marry in a simple registry in Bangalore followed by a dinner for 40 people in Malleshwaram
timeline.2017: Move to their first rented 2BHK in Richmond Town; optimistic, hard-working, mutually supportive
timeline.2020: Pandemic lockdown reveals cracks: the silence becomes thick; career anxieties compound
timeline.2022: Lease the 3BHK flat on 12th Main, Indiranagar (₹68,000/month); the middle 12x14 ft room is designated 'the studio/nursery'
timeline.2023: Two failed IUI cycles; they decide to stop without formally discussing whether they are stopping forever
timeline.2024: The middle room becomes a storage room: unopened cardboard boxes, an unstrung tanpura, architectural samples, silence
timeline.2025 (Present Story Year): The lease renewal notice arrives from landlord Mr. Vishwanathan. They have 60 days to either commit to two more years or end the tenancy.

theMiddleRoom.dimensions: 12 feet by 14 feet with east-facing clerestory windows
contents: A teak bookshelf with half-unpacked monographs on Deccan architecture and Mughal dyes
An unstrung Miraj tanpura in a quilted black canvas bag gifted by Nandini's mother
Nine sealed brown cartons from their 2022 move containing duplicate kitchenware and old journals
A drafting table with a green cutting mat covered in dust
A clothes drying rack frequently left standing with damp laundry
theMiddleRoom.symbolicWeight: Neither inhabited nor cleared. A buffer zone between their separate bedrooms; the physical manifestation of what they have not dared to decide.

relationshipArc.opening: Polite domestic mechanics: morning pour-over coffee, synchronized bathroom turns, grocery lists shared on Google Keep without conversation
relationshipArc.incitingIncident: Mr. Vishwanathan asks for an 8% rent hike and a signed two-year agreement; Nandini receives a 6-month conservation residency offer in Pondicherry
relationshipArc.risingTension: A work trip together to Karaikudi to document a 1912 Chettinad courtyard home; being outside their Bangalore flat strips away their protective routines
relationshipArc.crisis: A late-night confrontation in the middle room after returning from Karaikudi, unpacking the cartons they avoided opening for three years
relationshipArc.turningPoint: Neither an explosive screaming match nor an artificial romantic reunion; the honest admission of exhaustion and mutual love without certainty
relationshipArc.ending: They do not know if the marriage will survive twenty more years, but they clear the middle room together, painting the walls off-white, opening the windows, and deciding to live in the same house without hiding.

recurringMotifs: The brass hygrometer measuring invisible ambient moisture
The 12x14 middle room doorway where both stop but rarely enter
The 1912 Chettinad courtyard with rainwater harvesting urns
The smell of cardamom water at 10 PM
The lease renewal agreement lying on the granite kitchen island
prohibitions: No melodrama, no shouting matches, no infidelity clichés
Neither spouse is a villain; both are decent, considerate, quietly exhausted people
No miracle baby or fake pregnancy plot twist
No easy Hollywood resolution; the ending must feel earned, fragile, and adult
